steps.say: The Sun is a star at the centre of our Solar System. Eight planets orbit it.
steps.show: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune

steps.say: The Earth spins once every 24 hours, which gives us day and night. It orbits the Sun once a year.
The Moon orbits the Earth in about a month. The Sun always lights up half of it.

figure.alt: The Sun, the Earth and the Moon.

steps.say: As the Moon moves, we see different amounts of its lit half. These are the phases of the Moon.
The Earth's axis is tilted. When your half leans towards the Sun, it is summer; when it leans away, it is winter.
Near the equator, in Indonesia, it is warm all year. Our seasons are the rainy season and the dry season.
Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun. Its thick layer of gases traps heat.

check.prompt: How long does the Earth take to orbit the Sun once?

options.why: One day is one spin of the Earth on its axis.
About a month is how long the Moon takes to orbit the Earth.
A week is not linked to any orbit.

hints: Orbiting means travelling all the way around.
One spin on the axis takes one day.
Think about how often your birthday comes round.
check.explanation: The Earth takes about 365 days, one year, to orbit the Sun once.

check.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?

options.why: Venus is the second planet from the Sun.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.

hints: It is the smallest of the eight planets.
It is named after a fast messenger in old Roman stories.
Think of the first word in My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Naming.
check.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, followed by Venus, Earth and Mars.
